content.thinking:
4000 random machines × all targets × all disabled combinations (up to 3 disabled) pass against the brute force.

Let me also run a fuzz with deeper disabled sets and larger machines (7-8 states) to be safe. And let me test the `hops` tie-break more (equal cost, different hop counts).

Actually, the brute force enumerates simple paths with up to n+1 edges, so it covers the (cost, hops, lex) comparison fully ✓.

Let me run a bigger fuzz round with a different seed and slightly bigger machines.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace/tmp && python3 - <<'EOF'
s=open('fuzz_state.py').read()
s=s.replace("random.seed(1234)","import os\nrandom.seed(int(os.environ.get('SEED','1234')))")
s=s.replace("for trial in range(4000):","import os as _o\nfor trial in range(int(_o.environ.get('TRIALS','4000'))):")
s=s.replace("    n = random.randint(1, 6)","    n = random.randint(1, int(_o.environ.get('MAXN','6')))")

for seed in 7 99 20240101; do SEED=$seed TRIALS=2500 MAXN=7 python3 fuzz_state.py 2>&1 | tail -3; done
